Aiyo, let me think about this year's plan. I'm getting old, 76 already, been doing this since I was a boy. My body doesn't move like before, but wheat and maize — I know them like my own hands.

**About the land and family**

I have 16.1 mu, all in wheat-maize rotation like most of us here. Two of my sons work in town now, only come back for busy days — harvest and planting. My old wife helps with small things. So really it's mostly me and some hired help when needed. We also pay for the combine to come, everyone does now, nobody cuts wheat by hand anymore.

**Wheat (winter crop)**

I planted wheat in early October last year, same as always. Right after the maize came off. I used the old variety my neighbor gave me seed for — 济麦 something, I forget the number, but it's been good. Saved some from last harvest so I didn't buy much new seed, just topped up a little.

For fertilizer, before planting I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — the 复合肥 with the three numbers on the bag. That's my base. Then when wheat is jointing in spring, around March, I put down urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. That's what my father taught and what works. Some young farmers use less now, say the extension man told them, but I don't want to risk my yield. A bag of urea is cheap compared to losing 50 kg of grain.

Irrigation — I water before planting to get good germination, then winter water in December if dry, then jointing water in spring, then one at filling if the sky doesn't give rain. So three or four times. Well water costs money for the electric and I share the well with neighbors, we take turns.

I expect maybe 450 kg per mu. Last year was decent, got about that. If heaven helps, more.

**Maize (summer crop)**

Right after wheat comes off in early June, we have to rush. The combine cuts wheat, then within a week the maize must go in. I don't till — no time, and tilling costs money. I use the no-till planter, the hired one, goes right through the wheat stubble. Everyone does this now.

I buy hybrid seed for maize — you can't save it, doesn't grow right next year. Costs more but there's no choice. Maybe 郑单 958 or whatever the shop has, the shopkeeper tells me what's selling.

Fertilizer for maize: compound fertilizer as starter when planting, about 30 kg per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage I topdress urea, maybe 12-15 kg per mu. Maize doesn't need as much as wheat in my experience.

Irrigation for maize — usually summer rains come, but last few years been drier. I plan one or two waterings if the rain is short, especially at tasseling. Can't let it dry at that stage.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once right after planting, the atrazine kind. Insects — if armyworm comes I spray, but I don't spray just in case. Costs too much.

I expect about 480 kg per mu for maize. It's usually a bit better than wheat.

**What I worry about**

Price of fertilizer keeps going up. Grain price doesn't go up the same. My sons tell me to rent out the land but I can't — this land fed our family for generations. As long as I can walk, I farm. If my back gets bad, I'll hire more help for spraying and fertilizer. The combine and planter I already hire.
